font.$description: Font family stacks. `sans` defaults to Inter (owner, 2026-11-14: a plain zero, where Atkinson Hyperlegible's slashed zero made dates and money read as code; Atkinson stays a reading-face choice); the user-selectable typeface axis (data-typeface) overrides --mc-font-sans at runtime in a later step. Faces are self-hosted (OFL) by the design-system/app; the stack falls back to the system UI stack until the web fonts load.

display.$description: The display serif for ceremonial edges only — page mastheads, matter-name captions, greeting headers. Never workflow cells or running text (the reading face governs those; the user typeface axis must not fight a decorative heading). Variable: opsz gives display sizes the optical cut.

blackletter.$description: The brand mark face (illuminated M / wordmark contexts) ONLY — a fixed glyph treated as artwork, never running text. A drawn SVG mark is the planned successor; this face is the launch stand-in the design language names.

font-size.$description: Type size scale, in rem so OS/browser text-size settings scale the whole UI (WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text; design language §4). Root baseline 16px. Named font-size (not text) so the generated --mc-font-size-* variables cannot collide with the semantic text COLOR roles (--mc-text-default etc.) — a size var in a color slot used to pass the purity gate and fail silently. Tailwind's text-* utilities still map here (the utility namespace is the template's concern, not the variable's).

3xl.$description: Display size — page mastheads and ceremonial headings (the serif register). Deliberately a big jump from 2xl: the scale contrast between a masthead and its metadata is part of the register's voice.

weight.$description: Font weights. `display` is deliberately off-grid (a variable-axis value between regular and medium) — the display serif carries authority without heaviness, and the non-default number is part of what reads as typeset rather than templated. It requires a variable font (font.display is one); static fallbacks round it.

tracking.$description: Letter spacing, in rem so it scales WITH the rem type scale under OS/browser text-size settings (px tracking would visibly tighten as the glyphs grow — defeating the same WCAG 1.4.4 accommodation the rem type scale serves). DTCG dimensions offer px|rem only (no em), so each tracked VOICE gets its own token pinned to the size that voice is set in.

caps.$description: The letterspaced-caps label voice (structural labels: column headers, group labels, eyebrows, status text). ~0.09em at the xs size the voice is set in; uppercase needs the air that lowercase gets from ascenders/descenders.

wordmark.$description: The brand wordmark's wide tracking (MAGNA CARTA beside the illuminated M). Wider than the caps voice — the wordmark is engraved lettering, not a data label.
